thread:
Priya: Quick sync — post-launch metrics are in. We saw a ~13% drop in CTR on the new assistant flow and a p99 error spike to ~1.6% during peak around 11:15 PST. Proposing a two-wave follow-up: (A) hotfix wave this week for crashers + high-severity JS bundle bug, (B) enhancement wave next sprint for UX tweaks and throttling. Reply with what you think must go in Wave A.

Ethan: Hotfix = anything causing user-facing errors or data loss. I'll triage the top 5 Sentry issues and flag which are regressions vs flaky. Need agreement on rollback policy vs patch-in-place.

Marina: From a UX lens — the CTR drop is concentrated where inline suggestions render. Quick mitigation: disable inline suggestions and show a lightweight "loading..." state. Low-risk and reversible.

Jonah: Support queue update: 42 tickets flagged as "regression", includes 3 high-priority Enterprise (AcmeCorp x3). They explicitly asked for a stability fix ASAP.

Ethan: Agreed prioritize AcmeCorp flows. I can implement a targeted canary that filters by org_id. Rough dev estimate: 1.5d for canary path + 0.5d for tests. Routing snippet below I can use for infra:
```
route_match: org_id == "acmecorp"
pool: us-west-2-fallback
```

Priya: Proposed decision: Wave A = crashers, AcmeCorp regressions, JS bundle fix, and frontend fallback to disable inline suggestions. Wave B = batching/latency work, telemetry improvements, and UX polish next sprint. Any objections?

Mei: Rollout policy suggestion — incremental canary 10% -> 30% -> 100% over 6 hours with auto-rollback if errors exceed +0.5% absolute. I can own the rollout orchestration and alerts.

Ethan: Quick ops note: Dedicated GPU pool is near 80% at peak; autoscale warm-up might exceed our 6h window. Recommend routing canary to lower-util region and throttling background jobs during rollout.

Priya: Good — plan: canary -> us-west-2 fallback pool, throttle noncritical jobs. Jonah, please prep a short customer comms template for AcmeCorp and other affected customers referencing the mitigation.

Jonah: Draft ready, will ping Acme contacts once canary starts. Will include the temporary disable-suggestions mitigation and ETA for full resolution.

QA Bot: CI regression summary: 18/120 tests failed — 12 known flaky, 6 new failures: (1) suggestion render mismatch, (2) API timeout on long prompts, (3) two integration tests for session recovery, (4) one auth edge-case. Full report: https://ci.redwood/example/196789

Marina: For the suggestion render mismatch we can add a frontend guard that avoids rendering suggestions if model payload doesn't match expected schema. Small change, low risk.

Ethan: Action items + owners: 1) Triage Sentry top5 (Ethan), 2) Canary routing config + throttle (Mei + Eng-Infra), 3) Frontend fallback to disable suggestions (Marina), 4) Customer comms (Jonah), 5) QA regression run after patch (QA Bot). Target: start canary EOD tomorrow.

Priya: If canary is healthy at +12h, we'll promote. If not, auto-rollback and open a postmortem. Metrics to watch: p50/p95 latency, error rate delta, customer session success rate, and request volume by org_id.

Mei: I'll create a dashboard and wire alerts for those metrics (alert thresholds: error rate +0.5% absolute, p95 latency +200ms).

Ethan: FYI — disabling inline suggestions increases server-side tokens slightly due to losing client-side cache hits. Expect ~2% cost bump short-term; acceptable tradeoff for stability.

Priya: Agreed. Prioritize minimal customer impact. Any other blockers? :thumbsup:

Marina: :thumbsup:

Jonah: :thumbsup:

Ethan: :thumbsup:

QA Bot: Post-patch verification tests queued.

Priya: I'll update the roadmap board: label selected tickets 'hotfix-this-week' and move remaining backlog items to 'enhancements-next-sprint'. Will follow up with a quick status check at 10am tomorrow.
